summary: MODEL_CHANGE_REQUIRED: the read_only.go delete-key update frees released ReadIndex entries; the reference, trace harness and Update view were updated and validated on fresh traces. Model checking found one update-attributed defect: a reused RequestCtx can be released by a heartbeat response generated before the request, giving a stale linearizable read when a newer leader has committed.
validation_limits: All BFS model-checking campaigns except reachability canaries stopped at planned time budgets with non-empty queues (LIMITED_COVERAGE); see spec/output/campaign-summary.md.
The inherited VIEW MCView omits fault counters, so bounded BFS runs that use it can miss paths needing the remaining counter budget; the S6b guided hunt runs without the VIEW.
Crash, Restart, LoseMessage and ReadyAdvance are not observable in the in-process harness and are covered only by model checking.
The specula CLI is not installed in this environment; specula ci-result could not be run and Part 4 confirmation was not delegated.

findings.title: Reused ReadIndex context is released by an acknowledgement that predates it (stale linearizable read)
findings.cause: readOnly.advance now deletes released requests (read_only.go:103), so addRequest accepts a previously used RequestCtx, while recvAck still matches heartbeat responses only by context and counts a response generated for the earlier use.
findings.trigger: Leader serves a read for ctx; one follower's response to that heartbeat is delayed; the caller reuses ctx after its ReadState is produced; the delayed response is delivered (stale value if a newer leader committed during a partition in between).
findings.consequence: The leader releases the new read without any acknowledgement generated after it was accepted; with a newer committed leader the ReadState index is below an index committed before the read began (stale linearizable read).

premises: A caller may reuse a RequestCtx after the ReadState for its previous use was produced (read_only.go:19-23 asks callers to differentiate states, e.g. with unique ids).
Heartbeat responses can be delayed and reordered.
